# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 7 — Fear God, Not the Devil

**1** "Fear the Lord," he said, "and keep his commandments. Keeping his commandments, you will be powerful in every deed, and your every deed will be incomparable. For fearing him you will do everything well. **2** This is the fear which you ought to have to be saved. But do not fear the devil. **3** For if you fear the Lord, you will have dominion over the devil, for there is no power in him. But in whom there is no power, there is neither fear to be had. **4** But in whom there is a glorious power, there is also fear of him. For everyone who has power, that one is feared; but he who has no power, has no power to be feared by anyone. **5** Fear then the deeds of the devil, for they are evil. And fearing the deeds of the Lord, keep his commandments and you will live to God. **6** I said to him, "Sir, I was strengthened when I heard these commandments; for I know that I shall be saved if I keep them." He replied, "You will be saved — you and all who keep these commandments of the Lord."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 7 is a brief but pointed mandate: fear God, not the devil. The theological reasoning: power determines legitimate fear. God has power; the devil has none. Therefore fear God (productive) not the devil (unproductive). This is the Shepherd's apophatic demonology.*
